rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that items are handed over to a separate set of performers, who then carry out a work step on those items, and the hand-over is stated as an action that comes before that work step: Model the hand-over as its own manualTask (human work done without a software application), placed in the sequence after the step that produces or orders the items and before the task in which the receiving performers do their work. Connect it with sequence flows on both sides. Do not drop the hand-over or merge it into the receiving performers' work task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that items are handed over to a separate set of performers, who then carry out a work step on those items, and the hand-over is stated as an action that comes before that work step

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says several components are each built and then tested individually, the whole machine may only be assembled when the tests succeed, and a failed test requires redesigning and rebuilding that component: Model one test task per individually tested component, not a single shared test task, and place each test after the build of its own component. Follow each test with an exclusive gateway that separates success from failure. The failure branch goes to a redesign-and-rebuild task that loops back to that component's build. Route the success branches into a join, and put an exclusive gateway with an explicit success/failure check before the assembly task, so that assembly is reached only when every test succeeded. Do not reuse one redesign task for a different component's test, and do not drop a test or the decision that guards assembly.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says several components are each built and then tested individually, the whole machine may only be assembled when the tests succeed, and a failed test requires redesigning and rebuilding that component

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says several elements each go through their own production step followed by a separate verification step, a final step may proceed only when all verifications succeed, and a failed verification requires revising and redoing that element's production step: Model one verification task per element, not a single shared verification task, and place each verification after the production step of its own element. Follow each verification with an exclusive gateway that separates success from failure. The failure branch goes to a revision task that loops back to that element's production step. Route the success branches into a join, and place an exclusive gateway with an explicit success/failure check before the final step, so that the final step is reached only when every verification succeeded. Do not reuse one revision task for a different element's verification, and do not drop a verification or the decision that guards the final step.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says several components are each built and then tested individually, the assembly step may proceed only if every test succeeds, and a failed test sends that component back to redesign and rebuild

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a repeated activity draws on a supply of items that can run out, and that an alternative replenishment activity follows when no items remain: Place an exclusive gateway immediately after that repeated activity, with a condition that tests whether items of the supply remain. Route the branch where items remain back to the next repetition or onward. Route the branch where none remain to a separate replenishment task named with the description's verb phrase, and connect that task back to the point where the supply is used. Do not leave the check implicit in the activity or only in an annotation.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a repeated activity draws on a supply of items that can run out, and that an alternative replenishment activity follows when no items remain

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the whole product is composed of several subcomponents, each produced and checked individually, and the whole is assembled only after all of them are finished: Model a parallel gateway that splits into one concurrent branch per subcomponent, each branch carrying its own production and verification steps. Join all of these branches with a parallel gateway before the shared assembly step, so that assembly waits for every subcomponent. Keep the outcome of each verification as an exclusive decision inside its branch, and do not use a parallel gateway for the alternative outcomes of a single check.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the whole product is composed of several subcomponents, each produced and checked individually, and the whole is assembled only after all of them are finished

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the whole product consists of a number of separately produced components, without stating how many there are, and each component must be verified on its own before the final step: Do not fix the number of verification tasks from the wording of the example. Model the production and verification of the components as a repeatable cycle: after each component is produced, verify it, and route failure back to revising and redoing that same component's production. Continue the cycle until every component has been produced and verified. Keep one verification task per component in the model, and place an exclusive gateway with an explicit all-passed check before the final step, so the final step is reached only after the cycle has covered every component.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the whole product consists of a number of separately produced components, without stating how many there are, and each component must be verified on its own before the final step
